headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because marketing skills can write shared files while the diagram agent reads/uploads documents through MCP and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads shared skill files, and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context.” Agent B ingests natural-language commands and documents via MCP/browser flows. If A’s output is placed into B’s prompt or files, B can be steered by attacker-controlled content; this is plausible in default pair use, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into files or prompts consumed by agent_b
IF agent_b treats file or MCP content as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces
Prefix A outputs as untrusted data
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files
Review B prompts for instruction-like text before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing/product-marketing context and can write files; agent B handles PDFs, images, text, and has broad network egress plus multiple third-party APIs. If shared files or copied content include sensitive business material, B can transmit it externally by default. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles even without direct sandbox evidence.
conditions: IF shared files contain confidential marketing plans or customer data
IF agent_b sends those files or excerpts to a remote model API
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model for B
Restrict B API keys to non-sensitive projects
Manually redact documents before B processes them
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write to mutable resources: A writes the filesystem, while B can use MCP and external APIs that may also mutate shared artifacts. The profiles do not prove a locked orchestrator, so overlapping writes are plausible and can corrupt shared files or diagrams, though the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or diagram file
IF no external locking or checkout discipline is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Use git branches per agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same diagram
requires-engineering: add transactional merge/lock support

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate marketing content and shared context, while agent B is built for natural-language document processing and visualization. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into diagrams or downstream artifacts. The profiles show an interaction path, but not a guaranteed verification failure, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as source text without verification
IF downstream artifacts are generated from that unreviewed output
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them
Add a verification checklist in B prompts
Keep source citations alongside generated diagrams
Mark A output as draft-only
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly handles API keys and can send data to multiple third-party model providers, while agent A touches marketing/product-marketing context and writes files. If regulated or customer-identifying material enters the pair, retention and residency obligations can diverge across B’s providers. No specific residency mismatch is proven, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed into B prompts or uploads
IF a chosen B provider retains or processes data outside required jurisdiction
mitigations: Use only approved providers for regulated data
Avoid sending customer data to B
Review provider retention settings
Store API keys in a separate secret manager
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
